case_name: Sandhya Jadhav v State of Maharashtra
respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

31 March 2006
Appeal (Cr.) 368 of 2006 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 6361 of 2005)
The Judgment was delivered by: Arijit Pasayat, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. Appellant calls in question legality of the judgment rendered by a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court Nagpur Bench disposing of two appeals; one filed by the appellant and the other by two co-accused person. Challenge was to the conviction recorded and sentence imposed by the 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur. Appellant was convicted for offence punishable u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC') and was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation.
Appellant was also convicted for offence punishable u/s. 325 read with S. 34 IPC along with the other co-accused Kawadu and Arun and all of them were sentenced to suffer RI for 5 years and to pay a fine of Rs.300/- with default stipulation. Co-
facts: The appellant was convicted for offence punishable u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation.

The occurrence took place in the course of sudden quarrel where the so-called eye-witness and the deceased were the aggressors; the right of private defence was available to her and in any event the occurrence took place in case of sudden quarrel and, therefore, S. 302 IPC have no application.
Appellant and co-accused persons were residing as tenants in the house of Govindrao Ghoradkar (PW-2).
On 6th June, 1990 at about 8.00 a.m. Govindrao Ghoradkar (PW-2) went to the accused persons for demanding house rent.

The accused persons in collusion with one another and in furtherance of their common intention assaulted Govindrao Ghoradkar (PW-2) and when his nephew Anand Ghoradkar (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') intervened in the matter to separate them, appellant Sandhya delivered a knife blow on the back of the deceased Anand and committed his murder.
On conclusion of the trial, the trial Court found the accused persons guilty of the charges, convicted and sentenced them which were matter of challenge in the two appeals before the High Court.
issues: The legality of the judgment rendered by a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court Nagpur Bench disposing of two appeals;
The conviction recorded and sentence imposed by the 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur;
The applicability of Exception 4 to S. 300 IPC in the case.
The correctness of the Trial Court's finding that the occurrence took place in the course of sudden quarrel where the so-called eye-witness and the deceased were the aggressors;
The applicability of S. 302 IPC in the case.
petitioner_arguments: Even if the accusations of the prosecution are accepted in toto a case u/s. 302 IPC is not made out, in view of the categorical findings recorded by the Trial Court and the High Court that the assaults were made in course of a quarrel and conviction should not have been done in terms of S. 302 IPC.
Exception 4 to S. 300 IPC is applicable.

The act was committed without premeditation, in a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel without the offender having taken undue advantage and not having acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
respondent_arguments: The Trial Court was justified in recording conviction u/s. 302 IPC and the High Court has rightly dismissed the appeal.
The case is covered by S. 302 IPC as there was no intention to kill as a single blow was allegedly given and, therefore, also S. 302 IPC had no application.
court_reasoning: There is no previous deliberation or determination to fight. A fight suddenly takes place, for which both parties are more or less to be blamed.
The homicide committed is then clearly not traceable to unilateral provocation, nor in such cases could the whole blame be placed on one side.
For if it were so, the Exception more appropriately applicable would be Exception 1.
There is mutual provocation and aggravation, and it is difficult to apportion the share of blame which attaches to each fighter.

The help of Exception 4 can be invoked if death is caused (a) without premeditation, (b) in a sudden fight; (c) without the offender's having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner; and (d) the fight must have been with the person killed.
To bring a case within Exception 4 all the ingredients mentioned in it must be found.
holding: The conviction is to be altered to S. 304 Part II IPC instead of S. 302 IPC as done by the Trial Court and affirmed by the High Court.
Custodial sentence of 7 years would meet the ends of justice.
